original.title: Level 1 to 8 Pangaea Guard Beast — Who Watches Your Night? 🌙
original.banner: Which Permian beast guards your night?
original.hook_vo: Pangaea, after dark. Pick something to stand guard.
original.art_direction: Rust-red floodplain under a dusty violet sky, low 24mm lens in dry grass, one glowing ember of a lightning fire.

options.label: Burrowing Diictodon
options.vo: Level one: a tiny grazer at its burrow.
options.image_prompt: Life reconstruction informed by the supplied Diictodon skull reference: one small smooth-skinned beaked grazer at a red-earth burrow entrance in the Permian. A close three-quarter head and shoulders view shows a short broad skull covered with matte grey-brown living skin. Its short upper and lower horny beaks meet at the front of the mouth; one small white canine tusk descends from each side of the upper jaw behind the beak. The visible near tusk points downward. A tiny flat ear opening lies flush with the skin behind the eye. Two sturdy front feet rest on the red earth at the bottom of the frame, the body extends inside the burrow. Dusty violet night background, soft neutral moon fill and a restrained warm amber reflection on the cheek. Use the source only as an anatomical guide; every visible surface is living tissue or natural earth.
options.art_direction: Close view of one small living beaked Diictodon at a red-earth burrow under the violet Permian night, warm amber cheek reflection.

options.label: Tree-climbing Suminia
options.vo: Level two: Suminia, clinging to a branch.
options.image_prompt: Complete side view of one small Suminia crouching horizontally on TOP of a thick conifer branch. Its entire compact slender body, elongated neck, broad short blunt head and long tapering curling tail are visible. All four slender legs bend naturally at their joints, and all four feet grip the upper bark with long clearly separated toes. Its belly rests just above the branch and its head faces left along the branch. The long tail curves along the branch behind it. Small rounded scales, natural muted grey-brown skin, a large dark eye, a clearly closed mouth. The branch crosses the lower middle of the frame, with open violet sky behind and a warm ember reflection on the bark. Rust-red Permian floodplain under a dusty violet night sky, neutral soft moon fill and a restrained warm ember accent, photoreal painterly natural-history reconstruction, vertical composition.
options.art_direction: A small four-legged Suminia crouches horizontally on top of a conifer branch with every foot gripping the bark and its long tail visible against the violet sky

options.label: Tusked Dicynodon
options.vo: Level three: a beak and two great tusks.
options.image_prompt: Life reconstruction informed by the supplied Dicynodon lacerticeps skull reference: a close three-quarter view of one living Dicynodon head and upper chest against a soft red-earth Permian floodplain. The broad short skull is covered in matte grey-brown leathery skin, with tiny flush ear openings. A prominent curved upper horny beak meets the lower beak at the front. Two long pale canine tusks descend from the left and right sides of the UPPER JAW behind the beak; both tusks are clearly visible, pointing down beside the lower jaw. A single broad neck descends to the low body outside the close frame. Muted violet night sky, neutral moon fill and a restrained warm amber cheek reflection. Use the source only as an anatomical guide; every visible surface is living tissue or natural landscape.
options.art_direction: A close living Dicynodon portrait displays the broad horny beak and two downward upper-jaw tusks against a violet Permian night with warm amber cheek light.

options.label: Bumpy Scutosaurus
options.vo: Level four: a walking tank of bony bumps.
options.image_prompt: One living Scutosaurus in a complete low side profile, standing on ALL FOUR short thick legs with its broad belly close to the ground. A heavy oval barrel-shaped torso, short neck, small broad blunt head and short stout tail form one continuous horizontal body silhouette. The head is much smaller than the torso. Low rounded bony knobs stud the skin of its broad back and flanks. Short blunt bony projections border the sides of the cheeks. Its small closed mouth has a blunt rounded muzzle. All four similarly sized weight-bearing feet are planted on the earth; the front legs and hind legs are equally sturdy. Natural grey-brown pebbled skin with a soft amber edge light. Rust-red Permian floodplain under a dusty violet night sky, neutral soft moon fill and a restrained warm ember accent, photoreal painterly natural-history reconstruction, vertical composition.
options.art_direction: Complete side profile of a broad low Scutosaurus with a small blunt head, bony skin knobs, short tail and four sturdy weight-bearing legs

options.label: Moschorhinus
options.vo: Level five: short snout, with a big bite.
options.image_prompt: Use the supplied Moschorhinus life-restoration head crop as the guide for its short blunt muzzle and broad deep head. Reconstruct one living Moschorhinus in a close side portrait at an ancient riverbank. The muzzle is short in front of the eye, with a broad rounded nose, small front incisors and one near-side upper canine descending immediately behind the incisors beside the nearly closed lower jaw. A small ear opening lies flush behind the eye. Natural matte grey-brown soft tissue is illustrative, with a thick low neck leaving the lower frame. Dusty violet Permian night and red earth replace the source background. Soft neutral moonlight and a restrained warm amber glow on the near cheek. Only the living animal and prehistoric nature fill the portrait.
options.art_direction: Side portrait of a living short-muzzled Moschorhinus with a visible near upper canine, red ancient riverbank, violet night and restrained amber cheek glow.

options.label: Rubidgea
options.vo: Level six: a massive skull, built for biting.
options.image_prompt: Reconstruct one living Rubidgea head in near-side profile using the supplied fossil holotype photograph as the skull-shape guide. Preserve its massive deep skull, short broad snout and thick bony brow over the small rear-set eye. Cover the bone in matte grey-brown natural living skin. A row of small front incisors precedes one long near upper canine descending from the upper jaw beside the closed lower jaw. The canine is a laterally flattened curved saber tooth, with its root inside the maxilla. The neck and low shoulders leave the lower side of the close portrait. A blurred red Permian ridge and dusty violet night replace all source plate areas. Neutral moon fill and restrained warm amber glow on the cheek. The complete final scene contains only living tissue and prehistoric natural landscape.
options.art_direction: Near-side portrait of the massive broad Rubidgea skull under living skin, one visible upper saber canine, red ridge, violet night and restrained amber cheek glow.

options.label: Young Inostrancevia
options.vo: Level seven: a young hunter, still learning.
options.image_prompt: Use the supplied living Inostrancevia head drawing as a shape guide. Paint one smaller young Inostrancevia in a left-facing side-profile head and shoulder portrait, peering out from sparse dry grass on an ancient red floodplain. Its elongated broad muzzle, large nostril, low oval eye and closed robust lower jaw have natural living grey-brown skin. A modest near upper saber canine descends beside the closed jaw. The neck continues into a low muscular shoulder leaving the lower right edge. Lean subadult proportions, small flush ear opening, neutral soft moonlight, dusty violet sky and restrained amber reflected light on the grass. Replace the drawing paper with the prehistoric habitat and realistic painterly tissue.
options.art_direction: Left-facing living young Inostrancevia head and shoulder among sparse grass, lean subadult proportions and a modest upper canine.

options.label: Adult Inostrancevia
options.vo: Level eight: the adult hunter with huge canines.
options.image_prompt: Use the supplied living Inostrancevia head drawing as a shape guide. Paint one large adult Inostrancevia in a low-angle three-quarter head portrait facing toward the right, above a bare rust-red natural ridge. The broad elongated muzzle and deep muscular cheek dominate the portrait. Its mouth is slightly open, with one huge curved near upper saber canine descending from the upper jaw beside the thick lower jaw, small lower teeth and a smaller far upper canine partially occluded. Matte dark grey living skin covers the complete head and thick neck; a small natural ear opening sits behind the rear-set eye. Neutral moonlight reveals the anatomy, with dusty violet sky and restrained amber reflected sky glow on the cheek. Replace the drawing paper with the prehistoric habitat and realistic painterly living tissue.
options.art_direction: Low-angle three-quarter living adult Inostrancevia head above a bare ridge, massive cheek and visible huge upper saber canine.

original.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 8, because this animal's longest canines could reach 15 centimetres. Probably your best bet for keeping everything else away.

fact.text: Inostrancevia, a gorgonopsian, had large canines, the longest of which could reach 15 cm.
fact.source_sentence: It also has very advanced dentition, possessing large canines, the longest of which can reach 15 cm (5.9 in) and which may have been used to shear the skin of prey.

original.description:
Long before dinosaurs, the top predators on Pangaea were sabre-toothed relatives of mammals. Eight Permian animals, from a shy burrower to the biggest gorgonopsian of all, and which one would really keep the night quiet.
